content:
maria: Heads up — since yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing a regression in TP all-reduce latency on 8xA100 runs. Step p50 up ~18% when per-rank message sizes are in the 4K-16K range.

alex: ugh. numbers? single-run or from perf harness?

maria: quick numbers from full-integ (batch=1, seq=2048, tp=8):
- baseline (old selector): step=312ms, allreduce avg=22ms
- new selector: step=368ms, allreduce avg=41ms
(averaged over 5 iters)

sam: that doubles the allreduce for those msg sizes. any nvprof/nccltrace?

maria: attached a short profiler snapshot (trimmed):
```
NCCL: allreduce_ring   12.6ms  (msgsize 64KB)
NCCL: allreduce_tree   39.8ms  (msgsize 8KB)
Host wait for GPU        6.4ms
Kernel-switch overhead   3.1ms
total step gap observed ~56ms
```

maria: timeline shows switch to tree algo for those small messages after kernel-selector decided tree is "better" for that shape. but on our topology tree ends up much higher latency.

leo: did we change the msgsize thresholds in the selector? I thought we only adjusted kernel batching heuristics.

maria: selector change was this PR: kernel-selector now picks tree for <32KB when interconnect hopcount>1 (intended for large fanout saves). but our TP layout (pipeline shards + tensor shards) increases hopcount artificially for contiguous ranks, so tree gets chosen even when ring would be faster.

sam: that matches. tree has more small-message overhead on our NIC config. can we force ring at runtime for a quick check?

jing: repro command I used:
```bash
./run_tp_integ.sh --tp-size 8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 \
  --nccl-env "NCCL_ALGO=ring;NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=8" \
  --dump-trace /tmp/trace.json
```
If you set `NCCL_ALGO=ring` the allreduce avg drops to ~18-20ms on the same runs.

benchbot: perf-harness results (auto-run 3111112200):
- old-selector: step 312ms (±8), allreduce 22ms
- new-selector: step 368ms (±12), allreduce 41ms
- new-selector + NCCL_ALGO=ring: step 328ms, allreduce 19ms
(reaction: :bar_chart:)

alex: so quick mitigation is to suppress tree choice for TP deployments or add a topology-aware override. but long-term we should update the selector cost model w/ measured hop penalties.

leo: could be interaction with KV cache too — when kvcache is warm we emit smaller fragments and more frequent kv-evict broadcasts that change effective msgshape. any kvcache traces?

maria: yes, with kvcache enabled the payloads break into ~8-12KB per-rank pieces. disabling kvcache (or increasing coalesce window) pushes us into 48KB pieces and ring gets chosen again. profiler snippet:
```
with kvcache: per-rank-frag=9KB -> tree chosen -> allreduce 40ms
w/o kvcache: per-rank-frag=48KB -> ring chosen -> allreduce 13ms
```

sam: interesting. maybe kernel-selector should consider "kvcache frag probability" or we should coalesce fragments before comm scheduling. coalesce window tweak seems low risk.

jing: suggested quick patch: in selector, add an early check: if topology==tp_sharded && hopcount>1 then apply measured_penalty factor and prefer ring for msgsize < 32KB. I can prototype.

alex: alternative simpler approach: add a runtime flag `--comm-override=prefer-ring` per-deployment until selector updated. would unblock customers.

maria: yea please add flag. also logging of chosen algo + reason in the metrics so we can alert when selector chooses tree on TP with msgsize < 32KB.

benchbot: opened regression ticket PERF-TP-472 with benchmark artifacts and nvprof traces: https://redwood.internal/perf/PRF-472 (cc @maria @alex) :memo:

leo: experiments I'd run:
1) force ring vs tree (done by j) to confirm perf delta across multiple hw sets (A100, A40)
2) sweep msgsize threshold in selector (8KB,16KB,32KB)
3) toggle kvcache coalesce window (default, +2x, +4x)
4) run with/without batching heuristics patch that delays kernel handoff by 2ms to let prefix KV coalescing finish

maria: I'll run 1 & 3 on our infra and post numbers. alex if you can add the runtime `--comm-override` flag that would be great.

alex: on it. will add flag + metric emission for chosen_comm and chosen_reason. PR by EOD.

sam: for long-term: we should incorporate a small microbench suite into selector CI that measures ring vs tree on our common topologies. selector shouldn't be purely model-based; topology measurement matters.

maria: agreed. adding to roadmap item. ping me when PR ready; I'll run full regressions and update PERF-TP-472. thanks folks :thumbsup:

alex: PR: https://redwood.internal/changes/12345 (draft) — added flag `--comm-override` and metric `runtime.comm.choice` :wrench:

jing: quick note: also check NCCL params like `NCCL_PROTO` and `NCCL_SHM_DISABLE` — on DGX-like nodes they change tree/ring behaviour. keep in mind for cross-hardware comparisons.

maria: good call. will include those envs in the experiment matrix.

benchbot: scheduled follow-up run in 30m to validate alex's flag on ci-gpu-04. will post results. :robot_face:

alex: thanks. if this ships we'll put a temporary note in release notes that kernel-selector change had TP impact and flag available to override.

maria: awesome. filing a quick internal KB entry for ops with the workaround steps and commands.

leo: :clap:
